Chandan Mallik .... Petitioner

Mr. U.R. Jena, Advocate
 -versus-
 State of Odisha .... Opposite Party

Mr. A. Pradhan, Asc
 Coram: Justice V. Narasingh
 Order
19.10.2023 Order No.
01. 1.
Heard learned counsel for the Petitioner and learned counsel for the State.

2. The Petitioner is an accused in connection with C.T. Spl. (POCSO) Case No.81 of 2023 pending in the Court of learned Additional District & Sessions Judge-cum-Spl. Court under POCSO Act, Jajpur,
arising out of Binjharpur P.S. Case No.631 of 2022 for commission of offence alleged under Sections 363/366/376(2)(n)/34 of IPC read with Section 6 of POCSO Act.

3. Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned Additional District & Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Jajpur by order dated 06.10.2023 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.

entities.text: Additional District & Sessions Judge-cum-Special Judge (POCSO), Jajpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 4. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the Petitioner is in custody since 27.07.2023 and as charge sheet has already been filed on 26.09.2023, he may be released on bail.
5. Learned counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail in view of 164 Cr.P.C. statement of the victim and also criminal antecedent of the Petitioner.

6. So far as criminal antecedent is concerned, learned counsel for the Petitioner submits that Petitioner is accused in Binjharpur P.S. Case No.159 of 2020, Binjharpur P.S. Case No.81 of 2021,
Binjharpur P.S. Case No.184 of 2021 and Binjharpur P.S. Case No.225 of 2021.

1 7.

entities.text: Chandan Mallik vs State Of Odisha .... Opposite Party
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is stated that the Petitioner has been released on bail in all the cases.

8. Perused the 164 Cr.P.C. statement of the victim.
9.
Considering the tenor thereof and period of custody and filing of charge sheet, this Court directs the Petitioner to be released on bail on such terms to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin.

10. Keeping in view the criminal antecedent of the Petitioner, additionally, it is directed that Petitioner shall appear before the jurisdictional police station once every week on such date and time to be fixed by the learned Court in seisin till conclusion of trial.
Certification of such appearance shall be submitted to the Court in seisin.
11. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
12. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rules.
(V. NARASINGH)
